This is quantified via z-scores and Brier scores, which indicate a significant deviation from expected performance. The root cause is the reliance on confidence alone rather than an independent model for ranking probability. The confidence-based derivation of ranking probability (P_ranking = confidence/100) is a direct consequence of the lack of an independent model, creating a feedback loop where confidence acts as both signal and proxy for quality. The unexecuted remedy specification further compounds the problem by leaving known issues unresolved. These primitives form a coherent system where calibration failure propagates through ranking logic, undermining trust in the system’s outputs. The failure mode manifests as a persistent misalignment between claimed and realized performance, particularly at high confidence levels. The dual nature of the system—relying on a scalar input while lacking a probabilistic correction mechanism—creates a singular point of failure that is difficult to detect without rigorous empirical validation.
